_about: Fixture for tests/standalone/manual_glossary_inflection.py (issue #255). Fifteen short English paragraphs that force distinct inflected outcomes for the glossary targets, plus the glossary itself and the stems the harness counts. Committed so runs months apart stay comparable: do not reword a paragraph without noting it in the PR that changes it.
_paragraphs_about: Shared by every target. Positions cover, for Russian: instrumental (1, 7), genitive plural (2, 5, 8), prepositional (3, 10, 14), dative (9), accusative (13), and derivation (4 and 12 need the denominal adjective 'магловский', 5/6/11/15 need the compound 'маглорождённый') - D3 widened the licence specifically to cover those last two kinds.
paragraphs: The professor spoke with three Muggles at the gate, and none of them realised what he was.
There were dozens of Muggles in the street below, and not one of them looked up.
They argued about a Horcrux for the better part of an hour, until the candles burned out.
He wore an ordinary Muggle coat and carried a Muggle newspaper folded under his arm.
The register listed the names of seventeen Muggle-borns, written in the same careful hand.
A Muggle-born student had won the duel, and the hall went very quiet.
The diary had become a Horcrux long before she ever found it at the back of the cupboard.
He counted six Horcruxes and still refused to believe there might be a seventh.
She explained the rules to a Muggle who had wandered in through the wrong door.
The report said nothing at all about the Muggles who had seen the flash over the river.
The little shop on the corner was run by a Muggle-born witch from Leeds.
Muggle money was useless here, and he had known it since the first morning.
He watched the Muggle cross the road and disappear into the fog.
They spoke of Horcruxes only in the lowest of whispers, and never after dark.
Two Muggles and a Muggle-born stood arguing beside the fountain while the Horcrux cooled in her pocket.

russian._about: The headline measurement of issue #255. Both families have a famous competing established Russian rendering, which is what the reporter counted (their split was 24/14).

families._note: The glossary stem also covers the derived forms маглорождённых and магловский, which is the point of D3. 'маггл' is not a substring of 'магл' (double г), and the harness attributes each word to its longest matching stem, so the two can never double-count.

turkish._about: Secondary arm, kept in this same file rather than a second fixture. Turkish is the empirical check on D3: 'keep the stem, inflect the ending' is false here, because a final voiceless stop voices before a vowel-initial suffix (Hortkuluk -> Hortkuluğu). The competing rendering to watch for is the model dropping the target and leaving the English term.

voicing._about: Correct: the k voices to ğ before a vowel-initial suffix. Incorrect: the unvoiced stem carries the suffix directly (Hortkuluku).
